t: Appropriations and funds made available and authority granted pursuant to this joint resolution shall remain available until (a) enactment into law of an appropriation for any project or activity provided for in this joint resolution, or (b) enactment of the applicable appropriation Act by both Houses without any provision for such project or activity, or (c) August 31, 1966, whichever first occurs.

fable.w: This section only sets how long continuing-resolution appropriations stay available, ending on enactment of an appropriation, enactment of an Act without such provision, or a fixed date. The only tempting hook is the reference to action by 'both Houses', but Congress is inside the federal government and enacting legislation is not consultation with outside parties. No outside party, hearing, comment period, rulemaking, advisory body, or right to sue is involved.
fable.s: Appropriations and funds made available and authority granted pursuant to this joint resolution shall remain available until (a) enactment into law of an appropriation for any project or activity provided for in this joint resolution

qwen_block.w: This section defines the expiration date for the availability of federal funds and authority. It does not involve any consultation, coordination, or interaction with parties outside the federal government (such as the public, states, or private entities) in the decision-making process. It is purely an internal administrative provision regarding budget authority.
qwen_block.s: Appropriations and funds made available and authority granted pursuant to this joint resolution shall remain available until (a) enactment into law of an appropriation for any project or activity provided for in this joint resolution, or (b) enactment of the applicable appropriation Act by both Houses without any provision for such project or activity, or (c) August 31, 1966, whichever first occurs.

opus.w: This clause only sets when funding under a continuing resolution ends: when an appropriation is enacted, when Congress passes the bill without the project, or on August 31, 1966. The only actors named are the two Houses of Congress, which are inside the federal government. No state, member of the public, expert, or other outside party is consulted, heard, or allowed to object or sue, so this is not participation.
opus.s: Appropriations and funds made available and authority granted pursuant to this joint resolution shall remain available until (a) enactment into law of an appropriation for any project or activity provided for in this joint resolution
opus.b: 1. **Reasoning.** The tempting reading is to treat "enactment of the applicable appropriation Act by both Houses" as a decision process that counts as participation. That fails because both Houses of Congress are inside the federal government. This clause only says how long continuing-resolution funding lasts. No outside party is consulted, given a hearing, or given a right to sue.

qwen_chat.w: This section solely defines the expiration date for the availability of appropriated funds. It does not mention any requirement for the federal government to consult with or coordinate with entities outside the federal government (such as states, tribes, or the public) before making a decision. The only actors mentioned are Congress and the executive branch (implied by the use of funds), which are inside the federal government.
qwen_chat.s: Appropriations and funds made available and authority granted pursuant to this joint resolution shall remain available until (a) enactment into law of an appropriation for any project or activity provided for in this joint resolution, or (b) enactment of the applicable appropriation Act by both Houses without any provision for such project or activity, or (c) August 31, 1966, whichever first occurs.
qwen_chat.b: Tempting-but-wrong reading: One might argue that because the funds are for projects, there is an implicit process involving outside parties. However, the text itself only describes the duration of funding availability and conditions related to congressional enactment. It contains no language regarding consultation, hearings, advisory boards, or public comment.
